instruction: Describe the public health challenges highlighted by this disease data. (Source: Health_Ministry_Annual_Report_25-26.pdf, Section Ref: 774-2)
output: Tobacco use presents significant public health challenges related to tuberculosis (TB). Smoking impairs ciliary function, weakening the body’s natural defense mechanisms against airborne pathogens. It also compromises macrophage response – reducing their ability to fight off infections – and lowers CD4 counts, which are crucial for immune cell activity. Consequently, active smoking elevates the risk of TB infection and increases the likelihood of progressing from an infected state to active TB disease. Furthermore, it contributes to TB recurrence. These factors underscore the need for interventions addressing both tobacco use and TB prevention strategies.

instruction: Explain the key statistics and figures presented in this text. (Source: 2017_India_State_Level_Disease_Burden_Initiative_Full_Report.pdf, Section Ref: 804-1)
output:
In 2016, the greatest proportion of Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) were attributed to age groups under 5 years old (6%), followed by 5-9 year olds (12%) and 10-14 year olds (12%). The percentage of DALYs remained consistent across 15 to 19 year olds (12%), 20-24 year olds (11%), and 25-29 year olds (9%).  From 30-34 years old, the proportion decreased to 8%, continuing a downward trend for age groups 35-39 (7%) and 40-44 (6%). DALYs were lowest among those aged 45-49 (5%), 50-54 (4%), and older adults over 60.  Specifically, the percentage of DALYs was less than 1% for individuals aged 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, and those 80+.

Between 1990 and 2016, there were significant shifts in the leading causes of death and disability. Data analysis ranked the top 15 causes of DALYs, both sexes, to determine how these rankings changed over this period.
